scenario: 面试官要求设计一个 Datadog/Prometheus 式监控平台，正在圈定 v1 的功能边界。
q: 监控平台的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选，只选真正在范围内的）
options: 从服务/机器摄取 CPU、内存、延迟、自定义计数器等指标
支持 dashboard 查询、过滤、聚合和时间范围展示
支持阈值和时间窗口的 alert rule，触发后发通知
提供日志聚合与全文检索
why: ingest、查询、告警、通知是 v1 范围；日志聚合与全文搜索被明确划到范围外，是另一个系统的问题。
why_en: The v1 scope is metric ingestion, querying, alerting, and notification, while log aggregation and full-text search are explicitly out of scope.
options_en: Ingest CPU, memory, latency, and custom counters from services.
Query and visualize metrics on dashboards with filters and time ranges.
Support threshold and time-window alert rules that trigger notifications.
Provide log aggregation and full-text search.
q_en: Which core functional requirements belong in the monitoring platform v1 scope?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to design a Datadog- or Prometheus-style monitoring platform and define the v1 feature scope.
optionExplanations: 这是指标数据的起点：agent 或服务把 CPU、内存、延迟等点上报进来，没有它整条管道无从谈起。
用户真正看到指标的地方：dashboard 要能按时间范围过滤和聚合，否则采集来的数据没处可看。
让系统从被动展示变主动发现故障：阈值加窗口触发的 alert rule 才能在没人盯着屏幕时报警。
全文检索日志内容是另一个产品（如 ELK）的职责，混进 v1 会让范围失控，本题明确排除。
optionExplanations_en: This is where the metric flow starts: agents push CPU, memory, and latency points in, so nothing downstream works without it.
This is where users actually see metrics: dashboards need time-range filtering and aggregation or the ingested data has nowhere to go.
This turns the platform from passive display into active detection: threshold-and-window alert rules page someone even when nobody is watching.
Full-text log search belongs to a separate product like an ELK stack; folding it into v1 would blow up scope, so it stays explicitly out.

scenario: 目标是能撑起 500k 服务器、5M metrics/s 摄取的监控平台，同时兼顾查询延迟和告警可靠性。
q: 监控平台的关键非功能需求有哪些？（多选）
options: 支持 500k 服务器、峰值 5M metrics/s 摄取
Dashboard 要强一致，任何旧数据都不可接受
Dashboard 跨天或跨周查询需在秒级返回
告警从指标发出到触发低于约 1 分钟
why: 摄取规模、查询延迟和告警时限是硬指标；dashboard 可接受最终一致，强一致不是本题要求。
why_en: Ingestion scale, query latency, and alert latency are hard requirements, while dashboards are allowed to be eventually consistent rather than strongly consistent.
options_en: Support 500k servers and a peak ingestion of 5M metrics per second.
Dashboards must be strongly consistent and never show stale data.
Dashboard queries spanning days or weeks should return within seconds.
Alerts should fire in under about one minute from metric emission.
q_en: Which non-functional requirements matter most for this monitoring platform?
scenario_en: The target platform must handle 500k servers and 5M metrics per second while keeping queries fast and alerts reliable.
optionExplanations: 这是压死单机写路径的量级：500k 台机器、峰值 5M/s，直接决定摄取层必须走批量和缓冲。
误把 dashboard 当账本：这类监控图允许短暂展示旧数据，强一致只是不必要的额外成本。
用户翻看历史趋势时忍不了转圈：这条约束逼着查询层必须靠 rollup 或缓存把长范围查询压到秒级。
决定告警评估必须多快：1 分钟这个上限直接约束了轮询间隔，或者要不要上流式评估。
optionExplanations_en: This is the load that would crush a single-node write path: 500k machines peaking at 5M/s forces batching and buffering into the ingestion layer.
This mistakes a monitoring chart for a ledger: dashboards can tolerate briefly stale data, so paying for strong consistency here is wasted cost.
Users won't wait on a spinner to see history: this constraint forces rollups or caching so long-range queries return in seconds.
This sets the clock alert evaluation must beat: a one-minute cap directly bounds the polling interval or whether streaming is worth it.

scenario: 监控平台要覆盖 500k 台服务器，每台每 10 秒上报约 100 个指标点，峰值可达约 5M metrics/s。
q: 这个摄取量级最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 必须走批量、缓冲和写优化存储，而不是逐点直连中心库
5M metrics/s 属于普通 CRUD 量级，单机关系库足够
这个量级下可以让每次上报都同步等数据库写完成
峰值只在活动期出现，可以按日均值做容量规划
why: 5M/s 远超单机 CRUD 能承受的量级，意味着摄取路径必须批量、缓冲、写优化，而不是同步直写。
why_en: At about five million metrics per second, the ingestion path needs batching, buffering, and write-optimized storage instead of synchronous direct writes.
options_en: It must use batching, buffering, and write-optimized storage instead of direct point writes.
5M metrics/s is ordinary CRUD scale; a single relational database is enough.
At this scale, every report can synchronously wait for the database write.
The peak only happens during events, so capacity can be planned around the daily average.
q_en: What design decision does this ingestion scale imply?
scenario_en: The monitoring platform covers 500k servers, each reporting about 100 metric points every 10 seconds, for a peak near 5M metrics per second.
optionExplanations: 这正是 5M/s 这个量级唯一撑得住的形态：批量攒点、缓冲吸收突刺，落地时走写优化存储。
把小规模机群的日常写入错当成了 500k 台机器的峰值写入，单机关系库在这个量级下秒变瓶颈。
同步等写完成会让每次上报都卡在数据库延迟上，5M/s 下这份等待会瞬间把请求队列堆爆。
峰值就是要扛住的那一刻，按日均值配置容量意味着高峰时直接顶不住，这不是容量规划该有的思路。
optionExplanations_en: This is the only shape that survives 5M/s: batch points, absorb spikes in a buffer, and land them through write-optimized storage.
This confuses a small fleet's steady load with a 500k-server peak; a single relational box becomes the bottleneck instantly at this volume.
Waiting for each write to commit ties every report to database latency, and at 5M/s that wait alone floods the request queue in seconds.
The peak is exactly the moment capacity has to survive; sizing off the daily average means the system falls over right when it matters most.

scenario: 每个 metric data point 约 100-200 bytes，峰值 5M metrics/s，原始写入量约 1GB/s。
q: 这个字节量级最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 1GB/s 在网络和存储层可以忽略，用什么线格式都一样
线格式和存储都要考虑压缩与批量；JSON 逐点发送在此量级下不现实
每个 point 应带上完整历史记录以减少请求数
字节量级只影响磁盘成本，不影响协议选择
why: 1GB/s 级别的写入量决定了线格式要能压缩批量传输，落地存储也要走列式压缩，纯 JSON 逐点发送撑不住。
why_en: At roughly one gigabyte per second, the wire format needs batching and compression, so sending raw JSON point by point will not hold up.
options_en: 1GB/s is negligible for networking and storage, so any wire format works the same.
Both the wire format and storage need compression and batching; sending raw JSON per point will not scale.
Each point should carry its full history to reduce the number of requests.
The byte volume only affects disk cost, not protocol choice.
q_en: What design decision does this byte volume imply?
scenario_en: Each metric data point is about 100 to 200 bytes, and at 5M metrics per second the raw write volume is roughly 1GB per second.
optionExplanations: 1GB/s 持续写入既吃满网卡带宽也吃满磁盘 IO，不是可以随意忽略的小数字，线格式选型必须认真对待。
这正是这个字节量级唯一站得住脚的判断：批量加压缩把冗余的 JSON 字段和逐点开销都摊掉。
让每个点携带全部历史会让单条消息体积暴涨，反而在这个吞吐下把带宽和存储都进一步撑爆。
线格式效率同时决定网络带宽、CPU 编解码开销和存储体积，不是只有磁盘成本这一项。
optionExplanations_en: Sustained 1GB/s saturates both NIC bandwidth and disk IO; it's not a number small enough to wave off, so wire format really matters.
This is the only call this byte volume supports: batching plus compression amortizes JSON's per-point overhead and redundant fields.
Attaching full history to every point balloons message size and pushes bandwidth and storage even further past their limits at this rate.
Wire format efficiency drives network bandwidth, CPU encode and decode cost, and storage footprint together, not just the disk bill.

q: 为什么“告警 1 分钟内触发”在监控系统里通常是合理目标？
options: 1 分钟只是行业惯例数字，没有技术原因
更快触发在技术上不可能，指标采集本身就要 1 分钟
通知渠道限制了告警最快只能 1 分钟发一次
很多告警基于滑动窗口或趋势，需要累积到足够数据才能判断
why: 生产告警常看一段时间的均值、p99 或持续违反，而不是单个瞬时点，所以需要先累积窗口内数据。
why_en: Many production alerts look at a moving average, p99, or a sustained breach rather than a single instant, so they need enough accumulated data first.
options_en: One minute is just a convention with no technical reason.
Faster firing is technically impossible because collection itself takes a minute.
Notification channels limit alerts to once per minute.
Many alerts evaluate moving windows or trends, so they need enough accumulated data first.
q_en: Why is firing an alert within one minute usually a reasonable monitoring target?
optionExplanations: 叫它惯例是在回避真正的原因：告警要等窗口攒够样本才能判断趋势，这不是随手定的数字。
采集本身可以做到秒级甚至更快，瓶颈从来不在数据怎么进来，而在评估窗口需要多久。
通知渠道通常能立刻发出单条消息，真正的限制点在评估逻辑而不是发送环节。
这才是根因：均值、p99 或持续违反类规则都要先攒够一段时间的数据，才能判断趋势是否成立。
optionExplanations_en: Calling it a convention dodges the real reason: alerts need a window of samples before they can judge a trend, it isn't an arbitrary pick.
Collection itself can run at seconds or faster; the bottleneck was never how fast data arrives, it's how long the evaluation window needs to be.
Notification channels can usually fire a single message instantly; the real limit sits in evaluation logic, not delivery.
This is the actual cause: average, p99, or sustained-breach rules all need enough accumulated data before a trend is real.

q: 监控平台的核心实体包括哪些？（多选）
options: Trace：分布式追踪里的 span 集合
Label：指标上的 key-value 维度
Series：同一 metric name + labels 的时间序列
Alert Rule 和 Dashboard：告警条件与展示面板
why: Label/Series/Alert Rule/Dashboard 是本设计的数据与配置实体；分布式追踪的 span/trace 属于另一个系统。
why_en: Labels, series, alert rules, and dashboards are the core data and configuration entities, while distributed tracing spans belong to a separate system.
options_en: Trace: the set of spans a distributed request passes through.
Label: a key-value dimension used to slice and filter a metric.
Series: the time-ordered sequence for one metric name and label set.
Alert Rule and Dashboard: the condition that fires notifications and the panels that visualize data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式追踪里一次请求经过的完整调用链。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trace is the full call chain a distributed request passes through.

termDefinitions.meaning: trace 中的一段调用记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A span is one recorded operation within a trace.

q_en: Which entities are core to a metrics monitoring platform?
optionExplanations: Trace 和 span 是分布式追踪系统的实体，记录一次请求经过的调用链，不属于本题这套指标监控设计。
Label 是挂在指标上的 key-value 维度，用来按 host、region 之类的属性切分和过滤同一个指标。
Series 是同一 metric name 加 labels 组合下的点按时间串起来的序列，是存储和查询的基本单位。
Alert Rule 定义触发条件，Dashboard 负责可视化，两者是用户配置和消费告警信息的入口。
optionExplanations_en: Traces and spans belong to a distributed-tracing system, recording a request's call chain, not this metrics-monitoring design.
A label is a key-value dimension attached to a metric, used to slice and filter it by attributes like host or region.
A series is the time-ordered sequence of points for one metric-name-and-label combination, the basic unit storage and queries work on.
Alert rules define trigger conditions and dashboards visualize data; together they're how users configure and consume alerts.

scenario: cpu_usage{host="server-1"}=0.75 是某一时刻的一次测量；同一 host 这些点连成的完整时间轴是另一个层级的东西。
q: Metric 和 Series 的关键区别是什么？
options: Metric 只用于告警，Series 只用于通知展示
Metric 是某一时刻的单点值，Series 是它随时间累积的序列
两者其实是同一个概念，只是叫法不一样而已
Metric 存用户身份信息，Series 存访问日志内容
why: Metric 是某个时间点的一次测量；Series 是同一 metric name + labels 组合下，这些测量随时间串成的完整序列。
why_en: A metric is one measurement at a point in time, while a series is the full time-ordered sequence of measurements for one metric-and-label combination.
tradeoff: 单点测量值 vs 随时间的完整序列
options_en: Metric is only for alerting, and series is only for notification display.
A metric is a single point value at an instant; a series is that value accumulated over time.
The two terms are actually the same concept, just called differently.
Metric stores user identity data, and series stores access logs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一 metric name + labels 随时间的点序列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A series is the time-ordered sequence of points for one metric name and label combination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 附加在指标上的 key-value 维度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A label is a key-value dimension attached to a metric.

q_en: What is the key difference between a metric point and a series?
scenario_en: cpu_usage{host="server-1"}=0.75 is one measurement at one instant; the same host over time forms a higher-level sequence.
optionExplanations: 把两者按用途（告警/通知）分家是错的：区分点不在谁用它，而在数据本身是单点还是序列。
cpu_usage{host="server-1"}=0.75 这一条是 metric；把 server-1 所有时刻的这类值串起来才是 series。
两者粒度不同不能互换：metric 是一个点，series 是这个点所在的完整时间轴，混用会让存储模型出错。
两者都是指标数据，不涉及用户身份或访问日志，那属于完全不同的数据域。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting them by use case, alerting versus display, is wrong; the real distinction is single point versus full sequence, not who consumes it.
cpu_usage{host="server-1"}=0.75 at one instant is the metric point; stringing every timestamp for that host together is the series.
They're different granularities, not synonyms: a metric is one point, a series is its whole timeline, and conflating them breaks the storage model.
Both hold metric data, not user identity or access logs; that belongs to an entirely different data domain.

q: 补全 cardinality explosion 的定义：
text: 每个唯一的 {{metric name + label values}} 组合都会形成一个 {{series}}；标签值组合失控时，series 数会爆炸。
why: series 数量决定索引、内存跟踪、写入吞吐和聚合查询成本，是监控系统的核心风险。
why_en: Cardinality explosion happens because each unique metric-name and label-value combination creates a separate series.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 metric 下唯一 series 的数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique series under one metric.

q_en: Complete the definition of cardinality explosion.

q: 把 metrics 平台的端到端数据流排好序：
steps: 用户通过 dashboard 查询并聚合指标
服务产生指标点并发送给平台
Alert rules 周期性或流式评估指标
平台摄取、校验并写入时间序列存储
触发后 Notification Service 发出通知
why: 主数据流从产生和存储开始，再被 dashboard 和 alert 两条读路径消费，最后进入通知。
why_en: Metrics are generated, ingested and stored, queried by dashboards, evaluated by alerts, and finally delivered as notifications.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Agent[Agent] --> Ingest[Ingestion]
Ingest --> Kafka[Kafka]
Kafka --> Writer[TSDB writer]
Writer --> TSDB[(TSDB)]
TSDB --> Query[Query API]
TSDB --> Alert[Alert evaluator]
q_en: Put the end-to-end metrics data flow in order.

scenario: Agent/服务要高吞吐发送指标，网络协议示例用 JSON 表达，但真实系统可换 protobuf。
q: 摄取 API 的形态应是什么？
options: GET /metrics/one-by-one 每个点一个请求
POST /metrics/ingest 批量提交 metrics 数组
DELETE /dashboards/all
POST /alerts/notifyOnly
why: 高吞吐指标必须批量提交，减少每点一次请求的开销；线格式可从 JSON 换成 protobuf。
why_en: Metric ingestion should batch many points into one POST request instead of one request per point, since JSON can later be swapped for a binary format like protobuf.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是小型内部工具，简单 JSON HTTP 批量接口已经足够。
tradeoff: 批量吞吐 vs 单点请求的实现简单性
options_en: GET /metrics/one-by-one, one request per data point.
POST /metrics/ingest with a batched array of metrics.
DELETE /dashboards/all.
POST /alerts/notifyOnly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种二进制序列化格式，比 JSON 更紧凑、编解码更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Protobuf is a binary serialization format that is more compact and faster to encode than JSON.

q_en: What should the ingestion API look like?
scenario_en: Agents or services need to send metrics at high throughput; JSON is shown for the API shape, but production systems may use protobuf.
optionExplanations: 每点一个请求在小规模调试脚本里能用，但 5M/s 下连接数和请求开销会先把系统拖垮。
把一批 metrics 打包进一次 POST，能把请求数摊薄到可控范围，是高吞吐摄取该有的形态。
这是删除接口，处理的是 dashboard 配置而不是摄取热路径，跟这道题的写入形态无关。
这个接口只负责发通知，不接收指标数据，摄取路径根本走不到这里。
optionExplanations_en: One request per point works fine in a small debug script, but at 5M/s the connection and request overhead crush the system first.
Batching a whole array of metrics into one POST amortizes the per-point request overhead, which is the shape high-throughput ingestion needs.
This is a delete endpoint for dashboard config, nothing to do with the ingestion hot path this question is about.
This endpoint only fires notifications; it never receives metric data, so it's not on the ingestion path at all.

scenario: Dashboard 需要按 PromQL-like DSL 查询某个时间范围内的聚合指标。
q: 查询 API 最贴近哪种形态？
options: POST /metrics/ingest，用于写入而非查询
GET /alerts/sendNow，用于手动触发通知
GET /metrics/query，按 DSL 表达过滤聚合和时间范围
DELETE /series，用于删除整条 series
why: 查询接口要能表达 metric 选择、label 过滤、聚合函数、时间范围和采样步长这五要素。
why_en: A metrics query API needs to express metric selection, label filters, aggregation, time range, and step size.
whenOtherWins: 如果只服务固定 dashboard，可以用预定义 query id 简化客户端请求。
tradeoff: 表达力（过滤/聚合/时间范围） vs 查询语法复杂度
options_en: POST /metrics/ingest, used for writing, not querying.
GET /alerts/sendNow, used to manually trigger a notification.
GET /metrics/query, expressing filters, aggregation, and time range via the DSL.
DELETE /series, used to delete an entire series.

termDefinitions.meaning: Prometheus 的查询语言，本设计的 DSL 参考对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PromQL is Prometheus's query language and the model for this design's query DSL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 领域特定查询语言，用来描述要取的指标和聚合方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DSL is a domain-specific query language used to describe which metrics to fetch and how to aggregate them.

q_en: Which shape best matches the query API?
scenario_en: A dashboard needs to query aggregated metrics over a time range using a PromQL-like DSL.
optionExplanations: 这是写入接口，处理的是指标上报而不是 dashboard 想问的“过去这段时间发生了什么”。
这是手动发通知的接口，表达不了 metric 选择、聚合函数这些查询才需要的语义。
这条路才能同时表达要哪个 metric、按什么 label 过滤、怎么聚合、多长时间范围和多大采样步长。
这是删除操作，会清掉整条 series 的数据，跟只读查询完全是两码事。
optionExplanations_en: This writes metric points, not answers the dashboard's real question of what happened over a time range.
This manually fires a notification; it can't express metric selection or aggregation, which is what querying needs.
This is the shape that can express metric choice, label filters, an aggregation function, a time range, and a step size all together.
This deletes an entire series' data, a destructive write, not a read-only query.

scenario: 用户要定义 p99 latency 超阈值并持续 5 分钟才通知的规则。
q: 告警规则 API 应包含哪些核心字段？
options: 整条规则只留了一个用于展示的邮件标题字符串字段而已
规则里只保留了一个用来装饰 dashboard 展示样式的颜色字段
规则配置里混进了一个完全不该出现的主机登录密码字段
含 name、query、for、notifications
why: Alert Rule 本质是查询条件、阈值、持续窗口和通知目标的组合，缺一个就无法完整定义一条规则。
why_en: An alert rule combines a metric query, a threshold, a duration, and notification targets.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则由代码配置管理，API 也可以变成配置同步入口。
tradeoff: 规则表达完整性 vs 配置字段的简洁性
options_en: The whole rule keeps only a display-only email subject-line string field.
The rule keeps only a color field used to style the dashboard's display.
The rule config has a login-password field mixed in that should never appear there.
It has name, query, for, notifications.
q_en: Which core fields should an alert rule API contain?
scenario_en: A user wants an alert that fires only when p99 latency stays above a threshold for five minutes.
optionExplanations: 标题字符串说明不了触发条件是什么、要持续多久，规则根本无法被系统执行。
颜色只是展示层的样式选项，跟规则要不要触发、发给谁完全无关。
登录密码不该出现在告警规则这种配置对象里，混进来是明显的安全设计错误。
name 认身份、query 定条件、for 定持续时间、notifications 定去处，四要素凑齐规则才可执行。
optionExplanations_en: A title string says nothing about the trigger condition or how long it must hold, so the system can't actually run the rule.
Color is purely a display style choice, unrelated to whether the rule fires or who gets notified.
A login password has no business in an alert rule config object; including it is a clear security design mistake.
name identifies it, query sets the condition, for sets the duration, notifications sets the target; all four make the rule executable.

q: 让所有服务器直接 POST 到 ingestion service，再由它直接写数据库，在 5M metrics/s 下会怎样？
options: 会自动获得无限吞吐，不受硬件限制
两端都会被写入洪峰压垮，因为没有缓冲和背压
告警延迟会立刻降到 0，不再有窗口等待
cardinality 爆炸问题会自动消失
why: 直接写没有缓冲、背压或重放能力，数据库会成为下游瓶颈，洪峰下两端都会被压垮。
why_en: Writing directly from servers to a database with no buffer offers no backpressure or replay, so both the ingestion service and the database get overwhelmed by write spikes.
options_en: It automatically gains unlimited throughput regardless of hardware.
Both ends get overwhelmed by the write spike because there is no buffer or backpressure.
Alert latency immediately drops to zero, with no more window waiting.
The cardinality explosion problem disappears automatically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 下游处理不过来时让上游放慢或缓冲，而不是直接丢数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure lets downstream slowness throttle or buffer upstream writers instead of dropping data outright.

q_en: What happens if all servers POST directly to ingestion and it writes straight to the database at 5M metrics/s?
optionExplanations: 去掉中间层不会凭空变出算力，硬件的连接数和写入吞吐上限依然摆在那里。
没有缓冲挡在中间，写入洪峰会同时打穿 ingestion service 和数据库，两端一起扛不住。
告警延迟由评估窗口决定，跟摄取路径怎么写没有关系，架构调整改变不了这一点。
cardinality 爆炸要靠写入路径的 label 策略专门控制，跟直连数据库这个改动毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Removing a layer doesn't conjure extra compute; hardware limits on connections and write throughput are still there.
With no buffer in between, a write spike slams both the ingestion service and the database at the same moment, and neither can absorb it.
Alert latency is set by the evaluation window, not by how ingestion writes; this architecture change doesn't touch that.
Cardinality control needs a dedicated label policy on the write path; direct-to-database writes have nothing to do with it.

q: 只在负载均衡器后面增加更多 ingestion service 实例，为什么还不够？
options: 会让负载均衡器无法分流请求
会导致所有实例都禁止批量发送
只扩展了入口，所有实例仍冲击同一个数据库
会让 Kafka 被直接删除
why: 横向扩容只解决入口的并发数，没有解决数据库的持久缓冲、消费者失败和重放问题。
why_en: Adding more ingestion instances only scales the entry point; every instance still writes to the same downstream database, so the bottleneck just moves, not disappears.
options_en: It would make the load balancer unable to distribute requests.
It would forbid every instance from batching sends.
It only scales the entry point; every instance still hits the same database.
It would delete Kafka outright.
q_en: Why is adding more ingestion service instances behind a load balancer still not enough?
optionExplanations: 负载均衡器天生就是用来分流的，加实例不会削弱它这个能力。
批量发送是每个实例自己的行为，跟实例数量多少完全没有关系。
多开几个 ingestion 实例只是扩宽了入口，它们最终还是把请求全部转给同一个数据库承接。
这一步的场景里还没有引入 Kafka，也谈不上被删除的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Load balancers exist to spread traffic; adding more instances doesn't weaken that ability.
Batching is each instance's own behavior, unrelated to how many instances are running.
Adding more ingestion instances only widens the front door; they all still forward writes to the same downstream database.
Kafka hasn't even been introduced at this stage of the design, so deleting it isn't the issue here.

scenario: 摄取流量有突刺，存储消费者可能变慢或重启，但不希望马上丢失指标。
q: ingestion service 和存储之间应加入什么？
options: 只用浏览器 localStorage 缓存
Kafka topic，按 series 分区
只跑一个单机 cron 定时任务
接一个用于媒体分发的图片 CDN
why: Kafka 提供持久缓冲、背压吸收和分区并行消费，把摄取和存储解耦，避免存储抖动直接冲击上游。
why_en: Kafka decouples ingestion from storage with durable buffering, backpressure handling, and partitioned parallel consumption.
whenOtherWins: 如果规模很小且允许丢点，直接写存储可以更简单。
tradeoff: 持久缓冲与背压 vs 直连存储的实现简单性
diagram:
flowchart LR
Agents[Agents] --> LB[Load balancer]
LB --> Ingest[Ingestion fleet]
Ingest --> Kafka[Kafka buffer]
Kafka --> Writers[TSDB writers]
Writers --> TSDB[(TSDB)]
options_en: Only browser localStorage caching.
A Kafka topic partitioned by series.
Only a single-machine cron job.
An image CDN meant for media distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式持久化消息队列，用于缓冲和解耦摄取与存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed durable message queue used to buffer and decouple ingestion from storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个 topic 切成多份，允许并行消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition splits a topic into pieces so consumers can process it in parallel.

q_en: What should sit between the ingestion service and storage?
scenario_en: Ingestion traffic has spikes, storage consumers can slow down or restart, and the system should not immediately lose metrics.
optionExplanations: localStorage 活在用户浏览器里，服务器之间的机器根本共享不到，管不了后端管道。
按 series 分区的持久队列能吸收存储端的抖动或重启，让摄取端不用等下游追上来。
单机定时任务没有持久化和并行消费能力，存储一旦变慢它自己先被堆积压垮。
CDN 是给静态媒体分发用的边缘缓存，不具备消息持久化和顺序消费的能力。
optionExplanations_en: localStorage lives in a user's browser, not shared across backend machines; it can't back a server-side pipeline.
A durable queue partitioned by series absorbs storage-side slowness or restarts, so ingestion doesn't have to wait on downstream catching up.
A single cron job has no durability or parallel consumption; the moment storage slows down, the job itself backs up and stalls.
A CDN is edge caching for static media distribution, with no durable message ordering or consumption model.

scenario: 500k 服务器每 10 秒产生大量指标，不想让中心 ingestion 层承接 5M 个单点请求。
q: 边缘侧应该部署什么？
options: 让每个业务进程各自建数据库连接
装一个面向用户的浏览器插件
让人工定期手工上传 CSV 文件
本地 agent，采集+缓冲+批量上报
why: Agent 把采集、局部缓冲和批量发送下沉到机器侧，能把中心请求数降一个数量级。
why_en: Local agents collect, buffer, and batch metrics at the edge, cutting the number of requests hitting the central ingestion service by roughly one order of magnitude.
whenOtherWins: 如果只监控少量服务，直接 SDK push 也可能足够。
tradeoff: 边缘批量降低中心压力 vs 500k 台机器的部署运维成本
options_en: Let every business process open its own database connection.
Install a browser extension aimed at end users.
Have someone manually upload CSV files on a schedule.
A local agent that collects, buffers, and batches uploads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跑在每台机器上的后台进程，负责本地采集和批量上报指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An agent or collector is a background process on each machine that collects and batches metrics locally before shipping them.

q_en: What should run on the edge side?
scenario_en: With 500k servers producing many metrics every 10 seconds, the central ingestion layer should not receive one request per metric point.
optionExplanations: 每个进程各自开连接会把连接数和故障耦合都放大到 500k 台机器规模，这本身就是新瓶颈。
浏览器插件只能采到用户端行为，采不到服务器内部的 CPU、内存这些系统指标。
人工上传 CSV 满足不了实时性，等人手动操作完，1 分钟告警目标早就错过了。
机器侧后台进程先本地攒点再批量上报，能把打到中心 ingestion 的请求数压低一个量级。
optionExplanations_en: Letting every process open its own connection multiplies connection count and failure coupling across 500k machines; a new bottleneck by itself.
A browser extension only sees client-side behavior; it can't collect server-internal metrics like CPU or memory.
Manual CSV uploads can't meet the realtime bar; by the time a human finishes, the one-minute alert target is already blown.
A background process on each machine buffers locally and ships in batches, cutting requests hitting central ingestion by an order of magnitude.

q: Kafka 缓冲的一个重要代价是什么？
options: 所有数据会因此变成强一致查询
运维复杂度会自动降到 0，不再需要人管
恢复后要追赶 backlog，容量不足会长期落后
消费者从此不能并行处理消息
why: 如果系统停摆 5 分钟，恢复后要处理这 5 分钟的积压；平时容量越接近满载，追赶所需时间越长。
why_en: If the system is down for five minutes, it comes back to a five-minute backlog, and the closer capacity runs to full during normal times, the longer it takes to catch up.
options_en: All data would suddenly become strongly consistent to query.
Operational complexity automatically drops to zero and no longer needs anyone managing it.
After recovery it must catch up on a backlog, and tight capacity means staying behind long-term.
Consumers can no longer process messages in parallel.

termDefinitions.meaning: 停机期间没被消费的消息堆积，恢复后需要额外时间处理完。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A backlog is the pile-up of unconsumed messages during downtime that must be processed after recovery.

scenario: Kafka 作为持久缓冲挡在摄取和存储之间，系统曾经短暂停摆过一段时间。
q_en: What is an important cost of using Kafka as a buffer?
scenario_en: Kafka is used as the durable buffer between ingestion and storage, and the system has just recovered from a short outage.
optionExplanations: 缓冲队列改变的是数据的持久性和顺序，不会让下游查询突然变成强一致读。
Kafka 本身还要维护 broker、分区和副本，运维工作量不会因为引入它就消失。
停机几分钟意味着积压了几分钟的消息，如果平时容量本就顶着上限跑，追平这段积压会拖很久。
分区正是并行消费的基础机制，引入 Kafka 反而是为了让消费能并行展开。
optionExplanations_en: A buffer changes durability and ordering, not whether downstream reads suddenly become strongly consistent.
Kafka itself still needs brokers, partitions, and replicas to run; adopting it doesn't make ops work disappear.
A few minutes of downtime means a few minutes of backlog, and if normal capacity already runs near the ceiling, catching up drags on for a while.
Partitions are exactly what enables parallel consumption; Kafka is adopted partly to make that parallelism possible.

scenario: 存储要承接 5M metrics/s、按时间范围扫描、压缩、保留策略和长期 rollup。
q: 比普通 Postgres 更适合的主存储是什么？
options: 继续用没有分区的单表 Postgres
专用时间序列数据库（TSDB）
把对象存储直接当查询引擎用
用 Redis 永久保存全部原始点
why: 时间序列数据库针对 append-only 写入、时间分区、列式压缩和内置 rollup 做了优化，正好匹配这类工作负载。
why_en: A time-series database is optimized for append-only writes, time-based partitioning, compression, and rollups, which fits this workload.
whenOtherWins: 小团队几百台机器、短保留周期时，Postgres 或 TimescaleDB 的简单方案可能足够。
tradeoff: 专用时序优化（写入/压缩/rollup） vs 通用关系库的灵活查询
options_en: Keep using a single unpartitioned Postgres table.
A dedicated time-series database (TSDB).
Use object storage directly as the query engine.
Keep all raw points in Redis permanently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 针对时间序列数据优化的数据库，擅长追加写入、时间分区和压缩。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-series database is optimized for time-stamped data, with strong support for append-only writes, time partitioning, and compression.

q_en: What primary storage is a better fit than plain Postgres?
scenario_en: Storage must absorb 5M metrics per second and support time-range scans, compression, retention policies, and long-term rollups.
optionExplanations: 单表没有时间分区，写入越堆越多之后，扫描和 retention 清理会先把它拖垮，只适合小规模原型。
这类专用数据库把追加写入、按时间分块存储、列式压缩这些能力焊进内核，还自带预聚合层，正好克住这类高吞吐时序负载。
对象存储擅长便宜地长期存 blob，但没有索引和低延迟聚合能力，撑不起交互式查询。
Redis 是内存 KV，适合缓存热点状态，拿它永久存全量原始点会让内存成本失控。
optionExplanations_en: A single unpartitioned table degrades as writes pile up; scans and retention cleanup wreck it, so it only fits a small prototype.
This kind of database bakes append-heavy writes, time-bucketed storage, and columnar compression into its core, plus built-in pre-aggregation, a natural fit for this high-throughput time-series load.
Object storage is cheap for long-term blobs but has no indexing or low-latency aggregation, so it can't back interactive queries.
Redis is an in-memory KV store great for hot state; using it to permanently hold every raw point blows up memory cost.

scenario: 小规模监控系统尝试把每个 metric point 作为一行存在 Postgres，并把 PromQL-like 查询翻译成 SQL。
q: 用 Postgres 单表存 metric point 在本设计规模下有什么问题？
options: SQL 语法本身无法表达任何时间范围
Postgres 完全不能存储 JSON 类型的 labels
Dashboard 场景其实不需要任何查询
写入量、长扫描和 retention 清理会压垮它
codeSample:
SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', timestamp) AS bucket, AVG(value)
FROM metrics
WHERE metric_name = 'cpu_usage' AND labels @> '{"region":"us-east"}'
  AND timestamp BETWEEN $start AND $end
GROUP BY bucket;
why: 这条 SQL 在小规模能跑，但 5M writes/s 的写入、长期扫描和按 retention 做 DELETE 会让 Postgres 迅速退化。
why_en: This query works at small scale, but the write rate, long-range scans, and retention deletes make Postgres unsuitable at this scale.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有几百台机器和短期数据，关系库加分区可能是可接受的起点。
tradeoff: 关系库的查询灵活性 vs 专用时序库在这个写入量下的可持续性
options_en: SQL syntax itself cannot express any time range.
Postgres cannot store JSON-typed labels at all.
Dashboards actually need no querying at all.
The write rate, long scans, and retention cleanup would overwhelm it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写入引发数据库内部多次实际写入，DELETE 类操作常见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification is when one logical write causes multiple physical writes inside the database, common with retention deletes.

q_en: What breaks when this design stores metric points in a single Postgres table at the target scale?
scenario_en: A small monitoring system tries to store each metric point as a Postgres row and translate PromQL-like queries into SQL.
optionExplanations: 示例查询里的 BETWEEN 子句已经在表达时间范围，SQL 语法从来不缺这个能力。
JSONB 类型正是 Postgres 存半结构化 labels 的常规做法，存储能力不是问题所在。
Dashboard 恰恰要靠这类查询把原始点聚合成图表，说不需要查询等于否定了整个用例。
真正的瓶颈是高频写入、长范围扫描和按保留策略做 DELETE 这三件事叠加在一起。
optionExplanations_en: The sample query's BETWEEN clause already expresses a time range; SQL has never lacked that capability.
JSONB is the standard way Postgres stores semi-structured labels; storage capability was never the issue.
Dashboards depend on exactly this kind of query to turn raw points into charts, so saying no query is needed denies the whole use case.
The real ceiling is high-frequency writes, long-range scans, and retention deletes stacking on top of each other.

q: 时间序列数据库适合 metrics 的原因有哪些？（多选，选出真正成立的）
options: append-only 写入优化
天生擅长跨表强 JOIN 查询
按时间分区，旧数据可整块丢弃
列式/时间序列压缩
why: append-only、时间分区、压缩是 TSDB 匹配指标写入模式的核心特性；强 JOIN 从来不是 TSDB 的强项。
why_en: Append-only writes, time partitioning, and compression are what make time-series databases fit metrics, while complex joins are not their strength.
options_en: Optimized for append-only writes.
It is naturally good at complex cross-table JOINs.
Time-based partitioning lets old chunks be dropped wholesale.
Columnar/time-series compression.
q_en: Why is a time-series database a good fit for metrics?
optionExplanations: 指标数据几乎只追加不更新，TSDB 针对这种写入模式做了专门优化，写入吞吐比通用库高得多。
复杂多表 JOIN 恰恰是 TSDB 的弱项，它的存储结构是为时序扫描而不是关系查询设计的。
按时间切块存储让过期数据可以整块删除，不用逐行扫描删除，retention 清理因此很轻。
同一时间序列的相邻值往往变化很小，列式或时序压缩利用这一点把存储体积压得很低。
optionExplanations_en: Metric data is almost purely append-only; TSDBs are optimized for exactly this write pattern, with far higher write throughput than general databases.
Complex multi-table JOINs are exactly where a TSDB is weak; its storage layout is built for time-range scans, not relational joins.
Storing data in time-based chunks lets expired data be dropped wholesale instead of scanned row by row, making retention cleanup cheap.
Adjacent values within the same series often barely change, and columnar or time-series compression exploits that to shrink storage a lot.

q: 补全 metrics 保留/rollup 策略示例：
text: 可保留 {{10 秒 raw}} 数据约 15 天，{{1 分钟 rollup}} 约 90 天，{{1 小时 rollup}} 约 1 年。
why: 越老的数据分辨率越低越合算：用更少的点换更快的长范围查询和更低的存储成本。
why_en: Older data is kept at lower resolution because fewer points make long-range queries faster and storage cheaper.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把高分辨率原始点预先聚合成低分辨率数据，用于长范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollup pre-aggregates high-resolution raw points into lower-resolution data for fast long-range queries.

q_en: Complete the example metrics retention and rollup strategy.

scenario: Dashboard 查询是突发、用户驱动、可能很贵；写入是持续、稳定、高吞吐。
q: 为什么要把 Query Service 放在 TSDB 前面并和写路径分离？
options: Query Service 能替代所有存储
写路径不能访问 Kafka
读写特征不同，可独立扩容、缓存和翻译 DSL
Dashboard 只能访问客户端缓存
why: 查询是突发、用户驱动、可能很贵；写入是持续、稳定、高吞吐；分离后各自能独立扩容、加缓存、做 DSL 翻译。
why_en: Reads are bursty and user-driven while writes are constant and high-throughput, so separating them lets each path scale, cache, and translate queries independently.
whenOtherWins: 小系统可以让 API Server 直接查 TSDB，但规模上读写拆分更清晰。
tradeoff: 读写路径独立扩容与缓存 vs 单一服务的实现简单性
options_en: The query service can replace all storage.
The write path cannot access Kafka.
Reads and writes have different characteristics, so each can scale, cache, and translate its DSL independently.
Dashboards can only read from client-side cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存储和查询时间序列数据的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB is a database specialized for storing and querying time-stamped data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 领域特定查询语言，本设计用它描述查询和聚合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DSL is a domain-specific language, used here to describe queries and aggregations.

q_en: Why put a Query Service in front of the TSDB and separate it from the write path?
scenario_en: Dashboard queries are bursty, user-driven, and potentially expensive, while writes are steady, continuous, and high-throughput.
optionExplanations: Query Service 只是查询入口，真正持久化数据的还是 TSDB，它替代不了存储本体。
写路径正是 Kafka 要服务的对象，摄取端持续往 Kafka 写数据，两者关系说反了。
读方向流量忽高忽低还可能很贵，写方向持续稳定走高吞吐，拆开两条路径才能各自扩容、加缓存、翻译 DSL。
客户端缓存只是本地临时副本，不能当权威数据源，dashboard 最终还是要打到后端查询层。
optionExplanations_en: Query Service is just the query entry point; the TSDB is still what actually persists data, so it can't replace storage itself.
The write path is exactly what Kafka serves; ingestion writes into Kafka continuously, so this has the relationship backwards.
One side of this is spiky and pricey, the other is steady and high-volume; splitting query and ingest paths lets each one scale, cache, and parse its own DSL on its own terms.
Client-side cache is just a local temporary copy, not the source of truth; dashboards still ultimately hit the backend query layer.

scenario: 需求只是 1 分钟内触发告警，且 dashboard 查询能力已经存在。
q: 首版 Alert Evaluator 最简单合理的方案是什么？
options: 首版就给所有规则接入流处理框架处理
定时轮询规则，调用 Query Service 评估
让 Slack 自己承担查询和判断触发的职责
只在有用户打开 dashboard 时才触发评估
why: alerts-as-scheduled-queries 简单、可解释，1 分钟延迟需求下轮询已经够用，这也是 Prometheus 周期性评估规则、再交给 Alertmanager 通知的做法。
why_en: Scheduled polling queries are simple and debuggable, and they are sufficient when a one-minute alert latency is acceptable, which is how Prometheus's alerting works.
whenOtherWins: 如果告警必须秒级响应或基于流式窗口，Flink 等 stream processing 更合适。
tradeoff: 轮询的简单可解释 vs 流处理的更低延迟
diagram:
flowchart LR
Rule[Alert rule] --> Scheduler[Evaluator loop]
Scheduler --> Query[Query Service]
Query --> TSDB[(TSDB)]
Scheduler --> State[Alert state]
State --> Notify[Notification]
options_en: The first version wires every rule straight into a stream-processing framework.
Periodically poll the rules and evaluate them via the Query Service.
Let Slack itself take on the responsibility of querying and judging triggers.
Only trigger evaluation when a user happens to open the dashboard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储指标数据的时间序列数据库，评估器要查询它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The TSDB is the time-series database that the alert evaluator queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: Prometheus 生态里负责对已触发告警做分组、去重、静默和路由通知的组件；规则评估本身由 Prometheus server 周期性完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Alertmanager is the Prometheus component that groups, deduplicates, silences, and routes alerts that have already fired; rule evaluation itself is done periodically by the Prometheus server.

q_en: What is the simplest reasonable first version of the Alert Evaluator?
scenario_en: The requirement is only to fire alerts within one minute, and the dashboard query capability already exists.
optionExplanations: 1 分钟延迟目标根本用不上流处理这种复杂度，首版就上 Flink 是过度设计。
定时轮询规则、复用已有的 Query Service 去评估，简单可解释，刚好卡在 1 分钟目标之内。
Slack 只是接收通知的渠道，没有能力也不该承担查询和判断规则是否触发的职责。
告警必须在没人看 dashboard 时也照常触发，绑定用户打开页面等于放弃了主动发现故障的能力。
optionExplanations_en: A one-minute latency target doesn't need streaming's complexity at all; reaching for Flink in v1 is over-engineering.
Scheduling periodic polls against the existing Query Service is simple, debuggable, and comfortably meets the one-minute target.
Slack is just a delivery channel; it has no business owning query logic or deciding whether a rule fired.
Alerts must fire even when nobody is looking at a dashboard; tying evaluation to page opens abandons proactive detection.

scenario: Alert Evaluator 发现规则违反，需要通知 Slack/PagerDuty，但外部 API 可能失败且需要去重分组。
q: 应该在中间增加什么组件？
options: 让 evaluator 直接同步调用所有外部 API
让 TSDB 直接负责发短信
加一层 Notification Service
靠客户端浏览器推送来通知
why: Notification Service 负责分组、去重、静默、升级和重试，把不可靠的外部 API 调用和告警评估逻辑解耦。
why_en: A notification service handles grouping, deduplication, silencing, escalation, and retries, decoupling flaky external APIs from alert evaluation.
whenOtherWins: 小型内部工具可以先直接调用 Slack，但要清楚这是可靠性弱点。
tradeoff: 解耦通知可靠性与评估逻辑 vs 直接调用的实现简单性
options_en: Let the evaluator call every external API synchronously.
Have the TSDB itself send text messages.
Add a notification service layer.
Rely on client-side browser push to notify.
q_en: What component should be added in the middle?
scenario_en: The Alert Evaluator detects a rule violation and needs to notify Slack or PagerDuty, but external APIs can fail and alerts need grouping and deduplication.
optionExplanations: 同步调用 Slack 或 PagerDuty 会让 evaluator 被外部 API 的延迟和失败直接拖住，评估器本身也会变慢。
TSDB 的职责是存取时间序列数据，发短信这种通知职责跟它完全不相关。
专门的通知层负责分组、去重、静默和失败重试，把外部渠道的不可靠性挡在评估逻辑之外。
on-call 人员不一定开着浏览器，依赖客户端推送在真正需要报警时反而最不可靠。
optionExplanations_en: A synchronous call to Slack or PagerDuty ties the evaluator directly to that API's latency and failures, slowing evaluation itself.
The TSDB's job is storing and reading time-series data; sending texts has nothing to do with it.
A dedicated notification layer owns grouping, deduplication, silencing, and retries, keeping flaky external channels out of evaluation logic.
On-call engineers don't always have a browser open; relying on client push is least reliable exactly when a page matters most.

q: 补全告警去重状态机：
text: Notification Service 跟踪 alert 是 {{firing}} 还是 {{resolved}}，只在状态从正常变 firing 或从 firing 变 resolved 时通知。
why: 如果 CPU 一直高，每分钟重复发送同一页会造成告警风暴；状态转换通知能抑制重复。
why_en: Tracking firing versus resolved state prevents repeated notifications for the same ongoing incident.
q_en: Complete the alert deduplication state machine.

q: Notification Service 通常负责哪些能力？（多选）
options: 按 cluster/service 等 label 分组
去重正在触发的相同告警
维护 silencing/maintenance window
在没有人值班时自动关闭所有告警
why: 分组、去重、静默是 Notification Service 的核心职责；自动关闭所有告警会制造盲区，不是文章描述的能力。
why_en: Grouping, deduplication, and silencing are the notification service's real responsibilities, while auto-disabling all alerts when no one is on call would create blind spots.
options_en: Group alerts by labels such as cluster or service.
Deduplicate an alert that is already firing.
Maintain silencing or maintenance windows.
Automatically disable all alerts when nobody is on call.
q_en: Which capabilities usually belong in the Notification Service?
optionExplanations: 把同一批 cluster 或 service 的相关告警合并成一条通知，能防止同一次故障刷屏式发送十几条消息。
同一个规则持续 firing 时只在状态变化那一刻通知，避免每轮评估都重复发同一条页。
维护窗口内主动静音已知的计划性变更，避免团队被自己制造的噪音淹没。
无人值班就自动关掉全部告警，等于在最该被看见的时刻主动制造盲区，这不是合理设计。
optionExplanations_en: Merging related alerts across a cluster or service into one notification stops a single incident from spamming a dozen separate pages.
Only notifying when firing state changes, not on every evaluation cycle, keeps one ongoing incident from paging repeatedly.
Silencing known, planned changes during a maintenance window keeps the team from drowning in noise it created itself.
Auto-disabling every alert with nobody on call creates a blind spot at exactly the moment visibility matters most, not a reasonable design.

scenario: 用户查询 30 天 CPU 趋势，只需要小时级趋势，不需要 10 秒级原始点。
q: Query Engine 应该优先读取什么？
options: 所有 10 秒 raw 点
1 小时 rollup
Alert Rule 表
Notification retry queue
why: 查询范围是 30 天、只要小时级趋势，用 1 小时 rollup 能把每条 series 的点数从数十万降到几百级。
why_en: For a thirty-day query that only needs hourly trends, reading the one-hour rollup cuts points per series from hundreds of thousands down to a few hundred.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户放大到最近几分钟排障，需要切回 raw 或更高分辨率数据。
tradeoff: 低分辨率换查询速度 vs 需要放大到细节时的精度损失
options_en: All raw ten-second points.
The one-hour rollup.
The alert rule table.
The notification retry queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先按更大时间粒度聚合好的指标数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollup is metric data pre-aggregated at a coarser time granularity.

q_en: What should the Query Engine read first?
scenario_en: A user queries a 30-day CPU trend and only needs hourly trend data, not raw 10-second samples.
optionExplanations: 原始点适合放大到分钟级排障，直接拿它扫 30 天会把点数堆到数十万级，查询会明显变慢。
用户只盯小时级趋势，读这一层预先算好的粗粒度汇总，能把要扫的点数从十万级砍到几百，秒回。
规则表存的是告警配置，不是 CPU 的时间序列样本，读它查不出趋势图。
重试队列存的是等待发送的通知任务，跟用户想看的历史 CPU 数值毫不相关。
optionExplanations_en: Raw points are for zooming into minute-level forensics; scanning 30 days of them stacks up hundreds of thousands of points and slows the query badly.
The user only needs an hourly trend, so reading that pre-computed coarse summary cuts the points scanned from hundreds of thousands down to a few hundred, and it returns fast.
The rule table stores alert config, not CPU time-series samples; reading it gives no trend chart at all.
The retry queue holds pending notification jobs, completely unrelated to the historical CPU numbers the user wants.

scenario: Dashboard 面板要在原始 10 秒粒度下扫 30 天数据；单 series 约 25.9 万点，1000 个 pod 的面板就要扫 2.59 亿行，约 25GB。
q: 30 天原始点查询规模最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 全量原始点扫描不会影响查询延迟，只影响存储成本
全量原始点扫描会让面板退化到分钟级，须靠 rollup 或缓存降点数
2.59 亿行对时间序列数据库来说可以直接一次性全表扫描
点数越多，索引会自动保证查询保持亚秒级
why: 扫描 2.59 亿行、约 25GB 数据，即使有索引也要顺序扫描聚合，响应时间会到分钟级，必须靠 rollup 或缓存降低实际扫描点数。
why_en: Scanning roughly 259 million rows and 25GB even with good indexes means sequential aggregation that takes minutes, so rollups or caching are needed to cut the actual points scanned.
options_en: Full raw-resolution scans do not affect query latency, only storage cost.
Full raw-resolution scans degrade panels to minutes, so rollups or caching must cut the points scanned.
259 million rows can be scanned in one full table pass for a time-series database.
More points automatically keep the query at sub-second latency thanks to indexing.
q_en: What design decision does a 30-day raw-point query at this scale imply?
scenario_en: A dashboard scans 30 days at raw 10-second granularity; one series has about 259k points, and a 1000-pod panel scans about 259M rows or 25GB.
optionExplanations: 扫描 2.59 亿行既要读磁盘也要在内存里聚合，这直接决定了查询要花多久，不只是存多贵的问题。
这正是这个规模唯一站得住的判断：不先用汇总层或缓存把真正要扫的点数砍下来，面板响应就会拖到分钟级。
即使是专门的时序库，全表扫描 2.59 亿行也要付出真实的顺序读和聚合时间，不能当成一次性无代价操作。
索引能加速定位起止范围，但扫描和聚合海量点的代价依然存在，不会因为有索引就自动变成亚秒级。
optionExplanations_en: Scanning 259M rows means real disk reads and in-memory aggregation; that directly sets query time, not just the storage bill.
This is the only judgment this scale supports: without a pre-aggregated layer or cache cutting down the points actually scanned, panel response drags into minutes.
Even a dedicated time-series database pays real sequential-read and aggregation cost scanning 259M rows; it's not a free one-shot operation.
Indexes speed up locating a range, but scanning and aggregating that many points still costs real time; indexing alone doesn't make it sub-second.

q: 为什么不能只存平均值 rollup 后再查询 p99 latency？
options: 平均值会自动包含 p99
p99 不需要任何数据
TSDB 不能保存数字
平均值丢掉分布信息，无法恢复百分位
why: 百分位需要完整分布信息；只存 avg 之后，10 秒窗口内的分布形状已经丢失，rollup 要存 histogram 或 sketch。
why_en: Percentiles need the full distribution, so once only the average is stored the shape of that window is gone; rollups need histograms or sketches instead.
options_en: The average automatically includes p99.
p99 needs no data at all.
The time-series database cannot store numbers.
An average discards distribution information, so percentiles cannot be recovered from it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种近似统计结构（如 t-digest），能在有限空间内估算分位数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sketch is an approximate data structure, such as a t-digest, that can estimate percentiles within limited memory.

q_en: Why can you not store only average rollups and later query p99 latency?
optionExplanations: 均值是把一堆数压成一个数，压缩过程本身就丢掉了分布形状，反推不出 p99 在哪。
计算任何百分位都需要样本或分布摘要作为输入，不存在不需要数据就能算出来的百分位。
TSDB 存数字完全没问题，问题出在只存了均值这一个统计量，而不是整条分布。
均值只留下一个数，那 10 秒里每个样本的分布形状已经不可逆地丢了，只能换成直方图或近似分位结构重新存。
optionExplanations_en: An average compresses many numbers into one, and that compression itself throws away the shape needed to find where p99 sits.
Computing any percentile needs samples or a distribution summary as input; there's no such thing as a percentile with zero data behind it.
TSDBs store numbers just fine; the real problem is storing only the average statistic instead of the full distribution.
An average collapses a window into one number; the shape of those ten seconds is irreversibly gone, so it has to be rebuilt as a histogram or an approximate-quantile structure instead.

scenario: Dashboard 查询大量重叠时间范围，例如相隔 10 秒刷新一次 30 天图表。
q: 最佳低延迟读优化是什么？
options: 每次刷新都全量重新扫描 raw 数据一遍
干脆把整个 dashboard 功能禁用掉
查询拆分：新近数据查库，历史数据读缓存/预计算结果
干脆把已有的告警规则全部删掉
why: 相邻查询覆盖几乎相同的历史区间，把新近数据和历史数据拆开查、历史部分走缓存/预计算，能让多数面板亚秒返回。
why_en: Adjacent dashboard queries cover almost the same historical range, so splitting fresh data from cached or precomputed historical data lets most panels return in under a second.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询完全即席且很少重复，rollup 比结果缓存更关键。
tradeoff: 缓存/预计算换低延迟 vs 额外的失效和内存管理成本
options_en: Fully re-scan raw data from scratch on every single refresh.
Just disable the entire dashboard feature outright.
Split the query: read fresh data from the database and historical data from cache or precomputed results.
Just delete all of the existing alert rules outright.
q_en: What is the best low-latency read optimization here?
scenario_en: Dashboard queries refresh every 10 seconds over a 30-day chart, so adjacent queries cover almost the same time range.
optionExplanations: 10 秒刷新一次还每次全扫，等于把同一段历史区间重复算了几百遍，白白浪费计算。
禁用功能是在回避问题，不是在优化延迟，用户失去了本来该有的能力。
相邻两次刷新看的历史区间几乎完全重叠，把稳定不变的历史部分缓存住只查新增的一小段就够了。
告警规则和 dashboard 的读延迟是两条独立路径，删掉规则改变不了查询要扫多少数据。
optionExplanations_en: Re-scanning everything every ten seconds recomputes the same historical range hundreds of times over; pure wasted work.
Disabling a feature dodges the problem instead of fixing latency, and users just lose a capability they should have.
Adjacent refreshes overlap on almost the same historical range, so caching the stable old part and only querying the fresh slice is enough.
Alert rules and dashboard read latency are separate paths; deleting rules doesn't change how much data a query has to scan.

q: Dashboard 查询结果缓存最棘手的问题是什么？
options: 缓存这种结构完全存不下数组
加缓存反而会让查询变慢
缓存命中会自动生成新的告警
修正历史数据要失效缓存，还要控制内存
why: 历史数据修正会让旧缓存变脏，必须主动失效受影响的 key；热门 dashboard 太多时缓存内存也要有上限和监控。
why_en: Backfills or corrections to historical data make cached results stale, so affected keys must be invalidated, and cache memory needs monitoring as popular dashboards accumulate.
options_en: Caching as a structure cannot hold arrays at all.
Adding a cache actually makes queries slower.
A cache hit automatically generates a new alert.
Correcting historical data must invalidate cache and control memory.
q_en: What is the hardest part of caching dashboard query results?
optionExplanations: 缓存存序列化后的数组或聚合结果完全没问题，这不是限制缓存要解决的真实难点。
加缓存的目标就是减少重复的后端读，命中缓存本该比每次都查数据库更快。
缓存命中只是返回已存好的结果，不会触发规则评估，也不会生成告警。
回填或修正历史数据会让相关缓存条目立刻过期变脏，必须主动失效对应 key，同时热门 dashboard 一多，缓存内存也要设上限监控。
optionExplanations_en: Caching serialized arrays or aggregated results works fine; that's not the actual hard part here.
The whole point of caching is fewer repeated backend reads; a hit should be faster than always hitting the database.
A cache hit just returns an already-computed result; it doesn't trigger rule evaluation or create an alert.
Backfilling or correcting historical data instantly makes matching cache entries stale, so those keys must be actively invalidated, and memory needs a monitored cap as popular dashboards pile up.

scenario: 10,000 条 alert rule 若每 15 秒轮询评估一次，产生约 670 次查询/秒，直接打在 TSDB 上。
q: 这个查询量级最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 670 QPS 对 TSDB 来说可以忽略不计，可以把轮询间隔继续调短
轮询频率提高会让 alert 查询与 dashboard、写入争抢 TSDB 资源
查询量级只取决于 dashboard，不受 alert rule 数量影响
更高频轮询能让告警变成强一致
why: 670 QPS 会叠加在 dashboard 查询和写入负载之上，轮询间隔越短这个竞争越明显，这正是考虑切换到 Flink 流式评估的动机之一。
why_en: 670 queries per second stacks on top of dashboard queries and ingestion writes, and shortening the polling interval only makes that contention worse, which is part of the motivation for stream-based evaluation.
options_en: 670 QPS is negligible for the TSDB, so the polling interval can keep shrinking.
Higher polling frequency makes alert queries compete with dashboard queries and writes for TSDB resources.
The query volume depends only on dashboards, not on the number of alert rules.
Faster polling makes alerting strongly consistent.
q_en: What design decision does this alert query volume imply?
scenario_en: Ten thousand alert rules evaluated every 15 seconds create about 670 queries per second directly against the TSDB.
optionExplanations: 670 QPS 已经是叠加在写入和 dashboard 之上的额外负载，继续调短间隔只会让这份负担线性变重。
这正是这个查询量级带出的判断：轮询越频繁，alert 查询就越明显地跟 dashboard 和写入抢 TSDB 资源。
规则数越多、轮询越频繁，打到 TSDB 的查询就越多，量级明显是由 alert rule 数量驱动的。
轮询频率只影响多久看一次数据，不会把最终一致的查询变成强一致读。
optionExplanations_en: 670 QPS is already extra load stacked on top of writes and dashboards; shortening the interval further only makes that burden grow linearly.
This is exactly what this volume implies: the more frequently rules poll, the more visibly alert queries compete with dashboards and writes for the TSDB.
More rules and tighter polling both push more queries at the TSDB; the volume is clearly driven by the number of alert rules.
Polling frequency only changes how often you look at the data; it never turns an eventually-consistent read into a strongly consistent one.

scenario: 部分关键告警必须秒级触发，不想等下一轮数据库轮询；指标已经经过 Kafka。
q: 更适合的告警评估方案是什么？
options: 把轮询间隔拉长到 1 小时
加 Flink 做 Kafka 的第二个流式消费者
让 Notification Service 改去扫数据库
把告警判断逻辑下放给客户端
why: 指标已经流经 Kafka，让 Flink 作为第二消费者维护窗口状态、流式评估，能把延迟从轮询周期降到秒级。
why_en: Since metrics already flow through Kafka, adding Flink as a second consumer to maintain windowed state and evaluate rules as data arrives cuts latency from a polling interval down to seconds.
whenOtherWins: 大多数普通告警用 30-60 秒轮询已足够，流处理只值得用于关键低延迟规则。
tradeoff: 流式评估的秒级延迟 vs 轮询的实现和运维简单性
diagram:
flowchart LR
Kafka[Metric stream] --> Flink[Stream evaluator]
Rules[Rule config] --> Flink
Flink --> State[Dedup state]
State --> Notify[Notification queue]
options_en: Stretch the polling interval out to one hour.
Add Flink as a second streaming consumer of Kafka.
Have the notification service scan the database instead.
Push the alert-judgment logic down to the client.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理框架，能维护窗口状态并对到达的数据实时计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing framework that can maintain windowed state and compute over data as it arrives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标已经写入的持久消息队列，Flink 可作为它的第二个消费者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is the durable message queue metrics already flow through, and Flink can read it as a second consumer.

q_en: What alert evaluation approach fits better here?
scenario_en: Some critical alerts must fire within seconds instead of waiting for the next database polling cycle, and metrics already flow through Kafka.
optionExplanations: 拉长间隔只会让告警更慢，跟场景要的秒级触发方向完全相反。
指标本来就会经过这条消息队列，接一个新的流处理消费者维护窗口状态、实时评估，延迟能从轮询周期降到秒级。
让 Notification Service 去扫数据库是把职责搞反了，它该负责发送而不是评估规则。
客户端环境不可控也不可信，把告警判断下放给它无法保证服务端事故被可靠发现。
optionExplanations_en: Stretching the interval only makes alerts slower, the opposite of the seconds-level firing this scenario needs.
Metrics already flow through this queue, so adding a new stream-processing consumer to maintain window state and evaluate in real time drops latency from a polling cycle to seconds.
Having the notification service scan the database mixes up responsibilities; it should deliver, not evaluate rules.
Client environments are uncontrolled and untrusted; pushing alert judgment there can't reliably catch server-side incidents.

q: 用 Flink 做流式告警后，新增的主要复杂度是什么？
options: 告警从此不再需要任何状态
Kafka 从此不能被多个消费者读取
规则要编译成算子，还要处理好状态恢复
TSDB 从此必须被删除
why: 流式窗口评估依赖内存状态，规则要编译成算子，节点失败、规则变更都要靠 checkpoint 正确恢复，比轮询复杂得多。
why_en: Stream alerting depends on in-memory window state, so rules must compile into operators and checkpointing must correctly handle node failures and rule updates, adding real complexity compared to polling.
options_en: Alerting no longer needs any state at all.
Kafka can no longer be read by multiple consumers.
Rules must compile into operators, and state recovery must be handled well.
The TSDB must now be deleted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理定期把内存状态存下来，节点失败后能从上次快照恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint periodically persists in-memory state so a failed node can resume from the last snapshot.

scenario: 已经引入 Flink 做流式告警评估，规则要在内存里维护窗口状态。
q_en: What main complexity does Flink add for streaming alert evaluation?
scenario_en: Flink has been introduced for streaming alert evaluation, and rules now maintain window state in memory.
optionExplanations: 流式窗口评估恰恰依赖内存里维护的状态，说不再需要状态正好说反了。
Kafka 天生支持多个消费者组并行读取，加一个 Flink 消费者不会削弱这个能力。
每条规则得先编译成算子并常驻内存，一旦节点崩溃或规则改动，全靠 checkpoint 快照把状态续上，这是轮询没有的新负担。
TSDB 仍然服务历史查询和 dashboard，流式告警只是多加了一条低延迟路径，不会取代它。
optionExplanations_en: Streaming window evaluation depends on exactly that in-memory state; saying it needs none has it backwards.
Kafka natively supports multiple consumer groups reading in parallel; adding a Flink consumer doesn't weaken that.
Each rule has to compile into an in-memory operator, and after a node crash or rule change, a checkpoint snapshot has to bring that state back; genuine new overhead polling never had.
The TSDB still serves historical queries and dashboards; streaming alerting just adds a low-latency path alongside it, not a replacement.

q: 这种单实例架构的最大问题是什么？
options: 组件数量太多，没法部署
每一段都是单点，故障会丢指标或通知
查询会因此自动变快
cardinality 会被自动限制
why: 单实例、单 broker、单节点意味着任意一段故障都会让指标丢失、告警停摆或通知失败，而监控系统恰恰最不能在事故时失明。
why_en: A single instance at every stage means any one failure can drop metrics, stop alerting, or lose notifications, which is exactly when a monitoring system cannot afford to go blind.
options_en: There are simply too many components to deploy.
Every stage is a single point, so a failure drops metrics or notifications.
Queries automatically become faster as a result.
Cardinality gets automatically constrained.
scenario: 整条链路目前只有一份 ingestion、一个 Kafka broker、一个 TSDB 节点和一个 alert service。
q_en: What is the biggest problem with this single-instance architecture?
scenario_en: The current pipeline has one ingestion service, one Kafka broker, one TSDB node, and one alert service.
optionExplanations: 问题不是组件数量本身，五六个组件正常都能部署，真正的风险在每个组件都只有一份。
ingestion、broker、TSDB 节点、alert service 各只有一份，任意一段挂掉都会让指标丢失或通知失败。
单实例架构没有冗余带来的额外算力，查询速度不会因此凭空变快。
cardinality 控制要靠专门的 policy 和计数机制，跟部署了几份实例毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: The issue isn't component count; five or six components deploy fine, the real risk is that each one exists as only a single copy.
With one ingestion instance, one broker, one TSDB node, and one alert service, any single failure drops metrics or breaks notifications.
A single-instance architecture has no redundancy adding extra compute, so queries don't get faster because of it.
Cardinality control needs a dedicated policy and counting mechanism, unrelated to how many instances are deployed.

q: 提高监控系统 HA 的合理手段包括哪些？（多选）
options: 多个 ingestion instances behind load balancer
把所有组件收进同一个可用区，减少跨区网络延迟
Kafka replicated partitions 和 ISR
TSDB 多节点复制/多节点写入
why: 冗余实例、复制分区和多节点存储让单点失败可以被顶住；把所有组件塞进同一可用区反而会让整个区故障时全灭。
why_en: Redundant instances, replicated partitions, and multi-node storage survive single failures, while packing everything into one availability zone would make a zone outage take down everything at once.
options_en: Multiple ingestion instances behind a load balancer.
Pack every component into one availability zone to cut network latency.
Kafka with replicated partitions and an in-sync replica set.
Multi-node replication or multi-node writes for the TSDB.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 的同步副本集合，只有跟上 leader 进度的副本才在其中。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ISR stands for in-sync replicas, the set of Kafka replicas that are caught up with the partition leader.

q_en: Which techniques are reasonable ways to improve HA for the monitoring system?
optionExplanations: 入口层多开几个实例并配负载均衡，单个实例挂掉时流量能自动转到其他实例。
把全部组件挤进一个可用区确实能省点跨区延迟，但也把这个区变成了新的单点，一区故障就全灭。
分区带副本、只让追上进度的副本进 ISR，broker 挂掉时能从副本里选出新 leader 继续服务。
存储层多节点复制或多点写入，单节点故障时数据依然在其他副本上可用。
optionExplanations_en: Running multiple ingestion instances behind a load balancer means traffic auto-shifts elsewhere when one instance dies.
Cramming every component into one availability zone does cut cross-zone latency, but it also makes that zone a single point that takes everything down with it.
Replicated partitions plus an in-sync replica set let a new leader get elected from a caught-up replica when a broker fails.
Multi-node replication or multi-node writes on the storage layer keep data available on other replicas when one node fails.

q: 把“让监控系统每步可恢复”的设计要点排好序：
steps: Alert events 先写入 Kafka 或持久队列，再调用外部通知
Agent 本地缓冲并在网络/ingestion 故障时重试
写入设计成幂等，避免重试产生重复点
Kafka 跨可用区复制，broker 丢失不丢数据
Alert/Flink 状态 checkpoint，处理器崩溃后可继续
why: 可恢复设计的核心是每一段都有缓冲、复制、幂等或 checkpoint，避免 in-flight 数据消失。
why_en: Resumability means each stage has buffering, replication, idempotency, or checkpoints so in-flight metrics and alerts survive failures.
tradeoff: 每段都有缓冲/复制/幂等/checkpoint 的可靠性 vs 更高的实现和运维复杂度
diagram:
flowchart TD
Ingest[Replicated ingest] --> Kafka[Replicated Kafka]
Kafka --> TSDB[Replicated TSDB]
TSDB --> Alert[Restartable alerting]
Alert --> Notify[Durable notifications]
q_en: Put the recovery design points for each monitoring step in order.

q: metrics 写入为什么要尽量幂等？
options: 会让所有查询都变成实时
可以直接替代 Kafka 的作用
重试时不应产生重复数据点或告警
会把已有的 labels 删掉
why: 高可用系统一定会重试；幂等 key 通常来自 series id + timestamp，让重复的写入或告警效果安全、不重复。
why_en: Highly available systems will inevitably retry, so idempotent writes, typically keyed by series id and timestamp, make repeated attempts safe instead of creating duplicate points or duplicate alerts.
options_en: It would make every query real-time.
It could directly replace what Kafka does.
Retries should not create duplicate metric points or alerts.
It would delete existing labels.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次，效果和执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation produces the same effect whether it runs once or is retried multiple times.

q_en: Why should metrics writes be as idempotent as possible?
optionExplanations: 幂等改变的是重复操作的效果，不会让查询从最终一致变成实时强一致。
幂等是写入层面的一个属性，不具备 Kafka 那种持久缓冲和消费能力，两者不能互相替代。
高可用系统免不了重试，用 series id 加 timestamp 之类的幂等 key 能保证重试不会写出重复的点或触发重复告警。
幂等只约束重复写入的效果，跟这次写入携带的 labels 内容完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Idempotency changes what a repeated operation does, not whether queries switch from eventually consistent to real-time strongly consistent.
Idempotency is a write-layer property with none of Kafka's durable buffering or consumption model; the two aren't interchangeable.
Highly available systems inevitably retry, and idempotency keys like series id plus timestamp guarantee a retry never writes a duplicate point or fires a duplicate alert.
Idempotency only constrains the effect of a repeated write; it has nothing to do with which labels that write carries.

q: 为什么不能只用同一个监控系统监控它自己？
options: 监控系统没法产生关于自己的指标
告警规则技术上不能引用自身
Dashboard 没法展示任何内部指标
自己故障时会连可见性一起丢，需要独立信号
why: 监控平台失效时正是最需要知道的时候；只靠它监控自己会在同一次故障里连可见性一起丢掉，所以需要独立的健康检查或外部信号。
why_en: The moment the monitoring platform itself fails is exactly when you most need to know, so relying only on itself loses visibility at the same time it is needed, which is why an independent watchdog or external signal matters.
options_en: The monitoring system cannot produce metrics about itself.
Alert rules technically cannot reference the system itself.
The dashboard cannot display any internal metrics.
When it fails, visibility disappears with it, so an independent signal is needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 独立于主系统之外、专门检查其健康状态的看门狗进程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watchdog is a process independent of the main system whose only job is to check that the main system is healthy.

q_en: Why can the monitoring system not rely only on itself to monitor itself?
optionExplanations: 监控系统完全能对自己发出 CPU、内存、错误率这些自监控指标，这不是限制所在。
告警规则技术上可以引用系统自身的指标，只是这样做仍然共享同一个故障域。
内部健康状况完全可以画进内部 dashboard，问题不在能不能展示。
监控平台自己挂掉的那一刻，恰恰是最需要报警的时刻，只靠自己会连这份可见性一起丢掉，必须有独立于它的健康信号。
optionExplanations_en: The monitoring system can absolutely emit self-monitoring metrics like its own CPU, memory, and error rate; that's not the limitation.
Alert rules technically can reference the system's own metrics; the real issue is they still share the same failure domain.
Internal health can absolutely be shown on an internal dashboard; the problem isn't whether it can be displayed.
The exact moment the monitoring platform fails is when you most need to know; relying only on itself loses visibility at the same time, so an independent health signal is required.

scenario: http_requests{host, region, endpoint, status_code, method} 在 1000 hosts、5 regions、200 endpoints、10 status、5 methods 下，标签组合理论上限约 5000 万。
q: 标签组合爆炸最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 5000 万种组合不会真的出现，可以不设上限
只要加内存，TSDB 就能无限吸收 series
必须在写入路径做 cardinality 控制，否则失控
组合数只影响查询，不影响写入路径
why: 标签组合的理论上限增长极快，即使实际出现的远少于理论值，也必须在写入路径就做 label allowlist 和 series cap，否则会失控。
why_en: The theoretical label combination count grows extremely fast, so even though far fewer actually appear, cardinality controls such as label allowlists and per-metric series caps must sit on the ingestion path or growth becomes unbounded.
options_en: Fifty million combinations will never really occur, so no cap is needed.
Just adding memory lets the TSDB absorb series without limit.
Cardinality controls must sit on the write path, or it goes out of control.
The combination count only affects queries, not the write path.
q_en: What design decision does this label-combination explosion imply?
scenario_en: http_requests{host, region, endpoint, status_code, method} has a theoretical upper bound near 50M label combinations with 1000 hosts, 5 regions, 200 endpoints, 10 statuses, and 5 methods.
optionExplanations: 实际出现的组合确实远少于理论上限，但没有上限意味着一次代码改动就能让 series 数失控暴涨。
内存只是把崩溃时间往后推，series 数量继续无界增长，加内存治标不治本。
标签的组合数会随维度数指数级增长，必须在写入路径就先卡住允许的标签集合和条数上限，不然一次改动就能捅出上百万条新 series。
每条新 series 都要在写入时被索引和分配存储，组合数直接冲击的正是写入路径，不只是查询。
optionExplanations_en: Actual combinations do stay far below the theoretical ceiling, but having no cap at all means one code change can send series count out of control.
More memory just delays the crash; series count keeps growing unbounded, so it treats the symptom, not the cause.
The number of label combinations grows exponentially with each dimension; without capping the allowed label set and count on the write path first, one code change can spawn millions of new series.
Every new series has to be indexed and allocated storage at write time, so combination count hits the write path directly, not just queries.

scenario: 摄取层需要阻止某个 metric 因新增高基数 label 或无限 label value 把 TSDB 打爆。
q: 应加入哪两个控制组件？
options: 接入 CDN 和对象存储做静态内容缓存分发
只在客户端浏览器里加一层 localStorage 缓存
Policy Store 定规则，Redis 数 series
只是多开几个用于查看的 dashboard 展示面板
why: Policy Store 定义每个 metric 的允许 label 和上限；Redis 在写入时快速判断新 series 是否超限。
why_en: A policy store defines each metric's allowed labels and series cap, while a Redis-based cardinality tracker checks on ingestion whether a point belongs to a new series that would exceed the cap.
whenOtherWins: 如果是小系统且 metric schema 完全受控，人工 review label 可能已经足够。
tradeoff: 集中策略+实时计数的控制力 vs 引入 Redis 查询的额外延迟
options_en: Add a CDN and object storage for static content caching and distribution.
Add just a layer of client-side browser localStorage caching.
Policy Store defines the rules, and Redis counts series.
Just create a few more dashboard panels for viewing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 metric 下唯一 series 的数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique series under one metric.

q_en: Which two control components should be added?
scenario_en: The ingestion layer must stop a metric from blowing up the TSDB through a new high-cardinality label or unbounded label value.
optionExplanations: CDN 和对象存储解决的是内容分发和便宜长期存储，管不到写入时是否要接受一个新 series。
浏览器端的本地缓存对服务器写入路径不可见，拦不住摄取层新增的高基数 series。
Policy Store 集中定义每个 metric 允许的 label 和条数上限，Redis 在写入路径实时核对这条是不是要超编，两者配合能在源头拦住爆炸。
开更多 dashboard 面板只是增加查看方式，完全不影响写入路径要不要接受一个新 series。
optionExplanations_en: CDNs and object storage solve content distribution and cheap long-term storage; neither touches whether a new series gets accepted at write time.
Browser-side local cache is invisible to the server write path; it can't block a high-cardinality series from reaching ingestion.

A policy store centrally defines each metric's allowed labels and count cap, while Redis checks in real time on the write path whether this point would push things over budget; together they stop the blowup at the source.
Adding more dashboard panels just changes how data is viewed; it has no effect on whether the write path accepts a new series.

q: 把 cardinality enforcement 的步骤排好序：
steps: 如果是新 series，检查是否超过该 metric 的 series cap
指标点到达 ingestion service
去掉不在 allowlist 中的 label key
对剩余 label 组合求 hash 得到 series id
未超 cap 则发布到 Kafka，超 cap 则丢弃并计数
why: 先规范 labels，再识别 series，最后按 policy 决定接收或丢弃。
why_en: Cardinality enforcement normalizes labels, identifies the series, checks limits, and then accepts or drops the point.
tradeoff: 在写路径实时拦截超限 series vs 增加摄取延迟和实现复杂度
q_en: Put the cardinality enforcement steps in order.

q: 某个 metric 超过 series cap 后，系统应该做什么？
options: 继续无限写入，直到 TSDB 崩溃
丢弃新 series 的点，计数并通知团队
把所有旧指标都删除
把所有 dashboard 都关掉
why: 超过 cap 后保护系统比保留每个点更重要：丢弃新 series 的点、计数到 dropped_metrics，并通知团队处理。
why_en: Once the cap is exceeded, protecting the system matters more than keeping every point, so the system drops points from the new series, increments a dropped-metrics counter, and notifies the owning team.
options_en: Keep writing without limits until the TSDB crashes.
Drop points from the new series, count them, and notify the team.
Delete all old metrics.
Turn off every dashboard.
q_en: What should the system do after a metric exceeds its series cap?
optionExplanations: 放任继续写只是把问题拖到 TSDB 真正崩溃那一刻，代价从可控变成了系统性故障。
只丢掉新 series 的点，把它计入专门的丢弃计数器，并通知负责团队，既护住了系统又不会把问题埋起来。
超限的是某个新 metric，删掉全部历史数据是完全不成比例的反应，会破坏已有的可观测性。
关掉全部 dashboard 只会让人看不见问题，写入路径的超限风险丝毫没有被解决。
optionExplanations_en: Letting writes continue unbounded just delays the problem until the TSDB actually crashes, turning a manageable cost into a systemic outage.
Only dropping points from the new series, counting them in a dedicated drop counter, and notifying the owning team protects the system without burying the problem.
Only one new metric exceeded the cap; wiping all historical data is a wildly disproportionate response that destroys existing observability.
Turning off every dashboard just makes the problem invisible; it does nothing to fix the overload risk on the write path.

scenario: 每个指标点都去 Redis 做 set membership check，在 5M/s 下延迟和成本都很高。
q: 可以怎么降低 Redis 往返？
options: 改成每个点同步查一次 Postgres
把所有 label 全部删掉
批量或用本地 Bloom filter 先过滤
把 cardinality 检查挪到 dashboard 端
why: 批量做 set membership check，或用本地 Bloom filter 先过滤掉明显已见过的 series，能显著减少打到 Redis 的请求数，同时保留集中 cap 判断。
why_en: Batching the membership checks, or using a local Bloom filter to pre-filter series that have clearly been seen before, cuts the number of Redis round trips while still keeping centralized cap enforcement.
whenOtherWins: 如果摄取量很低，直接 Redis 查询更简单且准确。
tradeoff: 本地近似过滤降低 Redis 往返 vs 假阳性带来的少量误判
options_en: Switch to synchronously querying Postgres for every point.
Delete all labels entirely.
Batch checks, or pre-filter with a local Bloom filter.
Move the cardinality check to the dashboard side.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种概率型数据结构，能快速判断一个元素肯定不存在或可能存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic data structure that can quickly say an element is definitely absent or possibly present.

q_en: How can the system reduce Redis round trips?
scenario_en: Every metric point currently checks Redis for set membership, which is too expensive at 5M points per second.
optionExplanations: 换成 Postgres 只是把高频远程调用换了个目标数据库，往返次数和延迟问题一点没减少。
删掉全部 label 确实不用再检查基数了，但也把按维度切片过滤指标的能力一起丢了。
本地先跑一层 Bloom filter，把大概率已经见过的老 series 挡在外面，真正可能是新的才打一次 Redis，往返次数大幅下降。
写入时就该拦住的超限 series，等到 dashboard 端才检查，早已经写进了存储，为时已晚。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping in Postgres just moves the same high-frequency remote call to a different database; the round-trip and latency problem stays exactly the same.
Deleting every label does avoid cardinality checks, but it also throws away the ability to slice and filter metrics by dimension.
Run a local Bloom filter first to screen out series that are very likely already known, so only genuinely-possibly-new ones need a Redis round trip; a big cut in traffic.
A series that should be blocked at write time, if only checked on the dashboard side, has already been written to storage; far too late.

scenario: Slack 或 PagerDuty API 临时失败，但告警已经触发，系统不应丢这次通知。
q: Notification path 应该如何保证可靠性？
options: 先落盘 alert event，再重试外部发送
同步调用外部 API，失败就直接丢弃
等用户自己刷新 dashboard 去发现
干脆把告警功能关掉
why: 先把 alert event 写入持久队列再发送，能把外部渠道的临时故障变成延迟重试，而不是直接丢掉这次告警。
why_en: Persisting the alert event before attempting external delivery turns a provider outage into a delayed retry instead of a lost page.
whenOtherWins: 非关键 FYI 通知可以降低重试等级，但 on-call page 应可靠投递。
tradeoff: 持久化重试的可靠性 vs 额外的队列和状态管理成本
diagram:
flowchart LR
Alert[Alert fires] --> Queue[Notification queue]
Queue --> Sender[Sender workers]
Sender --> Channel[Email or Pager]
Sender --> Retry[Retry with backoff]
options_en: Persist the alert event first, then retry external delivery.
Call the external API synchronously and drop it on failure.
Wait for the user to refresh the dashboard and discover it.
Just turn alerting off entirely.
q_en: How should the notification path guarantee reliability?
scenario_en: Slack or PagerDuty can fail temporarily, but once an alert has fired, the system should not lose that notification.
optionExplanations: 把这次 alert event 落盘进持久队列，再去调用外部 API，Slack 掉线时也只是排队重试，事件本身不会丢。
外部调用失败就直接丢弃，等于把一次真实的事故信号彻底吞掉，没有任何补救机会。
指望用户自己刷新页面去发现事故太被动，等同于放弃了主动报警这个需求本身。
关掉整个告警功能是彻底放弃需求，而不是在解决外部渠道偶发失败这个具体问题。
optionExplanations_en: Persist this alert event to a durable queue first, then call the external API; a Slack outage just means a queued retry, and the event itself is never lost.
Dropping on failure silently swallows a real incident signal with no chance to recover it later.
Hoping a user refreshes the dashboard to discover an incident is far too passive; it abandons the whole point of proactive alerting.
Turning alerting off entirely abandons the requirement instead of solving the actual problem of an occasionally-failing external channel.

q: Dashboard 查询和 alert evaluation 在一致性要求上有什么区别？
options: Dashboard 要强一致，alert 可以随便丢
两者都完全不需要任何存储
两者都只能从浏览器缓存里读数据
Dashboard 可最终一致，alert 要可靠低延迟
why: 用户看图能接受短暂延迟，属于最终一致；但告警漏发或长时间延迟会直接拖慢事故响应，必须可靠且低延迟。
why_en: Users can tolerate a dashboard being slightly stale, so it can be eventually consistent, but a missed or delayed alert directly slows incident response, so alerting must be reliable and low-latency.

q: 指标晚到或乱序时，系统需要优雅处理，否则会怎样？
options: 所有数据反而会自动变得更准确
Kafka 从此没法存储任何消息
Dashboard 或告警窗口可能判断出错
标签数量会因此自动变少
why: 网络延迟和 agent 本地缓冲会让指标晚到或乱序；如果查询和告警窗口不允许一定迟到或做修正，图表会缺点、告警窗口判断也会出错。
why_en: Network delays and agent-side buffering can make metrics arrive late or out of order, so unless queries and alert windows tolerate some lateness or apply corrections, dashboards can show gaps and alert windows can misjudge.
options_en: All data would somehow automatically become more accurate.
Kafka can no longer store any messages at all.
Dashboards or alert windows can misjudge as a result.
The number of labels automatically decreases because of it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标到达系统的顺序和它们实际产生的时间顺序不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Out-of-order data means metrics arrive at the system in a different sequence than the order in which they were actually generated.

q_en: What goes wrong if the system does not handle late or out-of-order metrics gracefully?
optionExplanations: 晚到或乱序只会让数据顺序变复杂，不会让测量值本身变得更准确。
晚到的点照样能正常写入 Kafka，这跟 Kafka 存储消息的能力没有关系。

optionExplanations_en: Arriving late or out of order only complicates ordering; it doesn't make the underlying measurement any more accurate.
A late point still writes into Kafka just fine; this has nothing to do with Kafka's ability to store messages.
If queries and alert windows can't tolerate some lateness or apply corrections, dashboards show gaps and alert windows can misjudge.
Late or out-of-order arrival changes timing, not how many labels a point carries.

q: 补全 metrics 分区策略：
text: Kafka topic 和 TSDB shard 通常可按 {{metric name}} 或 {{metric name + labels 的 hash}} 分区，以便同一 series 的点被稳定路由。
why: 稳定分区让同一 series 的写入、压缩和窗口处理更容易并行且保持局部性。
why_en: Partitioning by metric name or series hash keeps related points together while enabling parallel ingestion and processing.
q_en: Complete the metrics partitioning strategy.

q: 补全 time-series storage 的写入特征：
text: Metrics 数据通常是 {{append-only}}、按时间写入、几乎不更新，因此适合 LSM 或 append-only 存储、时间分区和压缩。
why: 这个特征是 TSDB 能比通用数据库更适合指标存储的根本原因之一。
why_en: Metrics are mostly append-only and time-ordered, which makes specialized time-series storage efficient.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种写优化的存储结构，先写内存再顺序刷盘合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a write-optimized storage structure that buffers writes in memory before flushing sorted files to disk.

q_en: Complete the write pattern of time-series storage.
